To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the development paradigm is a product of the'modern' era, which has been deconstructed by the 'post-modern' or poststructuralist era; (2) the 'post-structuralist' or postmodern era has been marked by a shift in focus from 'knowledge economy' to 'knowledge ecology'; and (3) 'knowledge ecology' is a prerequisite to strike a right balance between 'development' and'sustainability'.

(a) sustainability is a science by its own right; (b) science & technology is a prerequisite for sustainable development; (c) sustainability is a means, not a goal; (d) sustainability is a value-based, inclusive and institutional science; (e) science & technology has been 'technological' in the name of sustainability; and (f) sustainability is a prerequisite for 'knowledge ecology'.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sustainable society, in particular with the development of an appropriate technology that will enable the transition to a sustainable society.

the following: (1) The development of a methodology to assess the sustainability of a product or service, and (2) The development of an information infrastructure to enable the assessment and communication of sustainability information.

the following: (i) to develop and validate a model for assessing the sustainability of development, (ii) to apply the model to a case study and to identify the critical factors, (iii) to identify the institutional and policy framework for sustainability, and (iv) to develop an integrated approach to sustainability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sustainability science is a new science, which is not merely a new branch of science or a new application of existing science.
, while science and technology have been instrumental in bringing about the present situation, they are also indispensable in the process of deconstruction of the present development paradigm.
the development paradigm is not only deconstructible but also deconstructing itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the science of sustainability should not be confused with science & technology, which are increasingly becoming technology-based, rather than science-based.
the science and technology paradigm is in need of a paradigm shift, which is not only a change of paradigm but also a paradigm change.
sustainability is a science by and in itself, and the science of sustainability has to be inclusive of values, responsibilities, institutions, instruments and knowledge ecology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sustainability is not a goal in itself but only a means.
the development paradigm is not only flawed but is also a major cause of ecological degradation and social injustice.
sustainability is a science in itself.
